note: BLM King Range NCA campground near the mouth of the Mattole River, at the end of Lighthouse Road about 6 mi from Petrolia (part of the road is unpaved). A short trail crosses the dunes to the beach; it is the northern trailhead of the Lost Coast Trail, elephant seals haul out on the shore, and the surf is dangerous for swimming. Two of the sites are equestrian sites in the same loop. --Claude
summary: BLM page + rec.gov (info-only 262790) + imagery read. $15 card-only kiosk, 8 people/2 vehicles; 23 sites incl. 2 equestrian; 24-ft trailer max; vault toilets, no water; year-round, FCFS. WATERFRONT: riverfront not supported (river mouth ~350-400 m north of the loop); coastal dunes recommended (sites behind the campground's own dune field, 600-ft trail to the beach). Pin ~100 m off, fine. Phone OK.
flags: WATERFRONT (riverfront -> coastal dunes recommended; riverfront not supported): on Esri imagery the loop (centre ~40.2897,-124.3557) sits on the inland edge of a hummocky vegetated dune field; the Mattole River estuary channel is ~350-400 m north of the loop's north tip, not 20-40 m as the stored evidence says (that evidence's 'open unused sand apron ~20-40m to the Mattole River mouth estuary/tidal flat' describes the dry backbeach, which carries no water in the imagery). BLM: 'a short 600-foot trail through sand dunes leads to the beach'; nothing but the dunes lies between the loop and the beach (trailhead/day-use parking is at the loop's south end, not between). That is the coastal-dunes case (the campground's own undeveloped dune field, campers walk through it to the beach). Site numbers can't be named (BLM posts site maps only at the kiosks). If AWH prefers not to move riverfront sideways without numbered sites, the default-down answer is coastal walk (ocean ~180 m on foot, no road between). Suggested evidence: 'BLM page 2026-11-27: "a short 600-foot trail through sand dunes leads to the beach"; Esri 2026-11-27: single loop on the inland edge of a vegetated wind-dune field, ~100-150 m of dunes then open beach, surf ~180 m W; river estuary ~350-400 m N of the loop; no road/lot/day-use between loop and beach -> coastal dunes.'

HORSE (Wildcat ruling: keep with caveat): BLM lists 'two equestrian sites' among the 23 in the single loop; their numbers and neighbours are not published online (site map only at the kiosks). The proposed note names the caveat.
